chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Kahmas, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you about the believer? He is the one upon whom the believers trust with their lives and their wealth. Shall I not inform you about the Muslim? He is the one from whom the Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand. And the emigrant is the one who emigrates from the evil deeds and leaves what Allah has prohibited. And the believer is sacred to the believer; he should not oppress him, abandon him, backbite him, or drive him away with a single push.'

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِن: The believer, one who has deep faith
key_terms.الْمُسْلِم: The Muslim, one who submits to God
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِر: The emigrant, one who leaves sin

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a true believer and Muslim according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, establishes a comprehensive taxonomy of spiritual maturity by distinguishing between the linguistic submission of a Muslim, the moral migration of a Mu'hajir, and the deep-seated faith of a Mu'min. It highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on social cohesion through the protection of a believer’s honor, wealth, and self from oppression, abandonment, and backbiting, reflecting the Shia focus on both individual piety and communal rights.
